bead.title: Couple terminal reap to the emission frontier and expose emission lag metrics
bead.description:
PROBLEM
A terminal item reaped before its terminal change record is durably emitted silently drops the terminal transition from downstream history — the subtlest correctness rule in TD-008. Separately, emission lag must be observable so operators can see history debt.

CURRENT STATE
- Terminal reap is governed by terminal_retention_ms alone (crates/pqueue-core/src/domain.rs:599,631; purge/tombstone paths in the relational stores).
- Debt-metric pattern to mirror: TD-004 async-apply debt metrics.
- Emission cursor lands with the engine foundation bead.

PROPOSED FIX
Per TD-008 Retention section: reap frontier = min(terminal_at + retention, emission_cursor_position) — a terminal item past retention is NOT reaped while the emission cursor is behind its terminal record; it becomes reapable once the cursor durably passes it. Queues with emit_change_records=false keep the pure retention frontier. Add emission_lag_commands and emission_oldest_unemitted_age_ms metrics, plus a resident-terminal-count metric so the 1h-retention memory cost is visible.

NON-SCOPE
- Sink/transport (sibling bead). Retention default change (already its own bead).
bead.acceptance:
1. reap_waits_for_emission: a terminal item past terminal_retention_ms is NOT reaped while the emission cursor is behind its position, and is reaped after the cursor passes. cargo test -p pqueue-projection reap_waits_for_emission
2. reap_ignores_emission_when_disabled: with emit_change_records=false the pure retention frontier applies. cargo test -p pqueue-projection reap_ignores_emission_when_disabled
3. Metrics assertions: emission lag and resident-terminal-count are observable and bounded in the test scenario.
4. cargo test -p pqueue-projection passes.
